Title: Example row - the shape of an owner decision brief
OneLine: the one-line form status.md projects - what is being decided, and the recommendation in a clause
Decision: What is being decided, who raised it and when, and any context a ruler needs that is not obvious from the one-line.
BlastRadius: What breaks or changes if this is ruled either way - the honest cost, not the optimistic one.
Options: Option (a) ... · Option (b) ... · Option (c) ... - each with its FOR and AGAINST, separated by the middot the other registries use for lists-in-cells.
Recommendation: The driver's recommendation and WHY, in the same voice a reviewer would argue it.

Title: WI-123: review-cadence dial

Title: Retire open-items.md for one generated HTML reference view
OneLine: rule whether open-items.md is retired outright for a single generated HTML owner surface - ruled (b): open-items.csv is the source, open-items.html is the view
Decision: Raised at the first re-attestation sitting: the generated pending projection was a POINTER where the owner needed the before/after, and the depth that makes a re-attest readable is a word-level diff, which markdown cannot express. The owner went further than the format question: -open-items.md is no longer even necessary; a single html reference view is sufficient, the md can be retired in its entirety.-
BlastRadius: Kit-wide, not local: OPEN_ITEMS.template.md is a bootstrap MAPPING destination (every adopting repo has one), 11 kit-doc references, 7 test modules, one SR/LLR/TC row, and agent_dispatch uses the file as a status-map marker while refreshing its pending block every dispatch loop. A kit version bump with a documented migration.
Options: (a) HTML view over per-item markdown sources - prose stays writable and diffable, but keeps a directory of prose files as a second authoring surface · (b) HTML view over a CSV registry - one registry, one view; OI state becomes queryable; prose authors into cells · (c) fold OI state into work-items.csv - blurs decision-vs-work · (d) keep the file and add HTML depth beside it - leaves two surfaces where the owner wants one.
Recommendation: Driver recommended (a); owner ruled (b), on the framing that settles the prose-in-cells objection: the briefs are pulled into the generator to construct the HTML, which is what a human actually references, so the CSV is a machine source read raw exactly as often as work-items.csv is - never.

Title: concurrency-v2 B2: strike or restate the specs-mirror-the-terminal-folders sentence
OneLine: RULED 2026-08-01: RESTATE (a) - executed the same date (B2 amended in place; the archive stays flat by decision; declared-absences lines restated). Original brief: rule whether concurrency-v2 B2's second sentence is STRUCK or RESTATED - a decision about the DESIGN TEXT only; WI-391, the row that would have built it, is already cancelled under either answer
Decision: SCOPE FIRST, because it is easy to misread: this rules on the SENTENCE, not on whether anything gets built. B2 says a closed WI's spec-of-record moves to docs/archive/specs/complete/ or docs/archive/specs/cancelled/ rather than one flat docs/archive/specs/, so a spec's location answers shipped-or-cancelled without opening it. WI-391 was filed to build that and instead refuted it on measurement; the refutation was independently confirmed (APPROVE findings=6, 2a4c9642). WI-391 is CANCELLED, not parked, because under BOTH options below its work does not happen - so a ruler here is choosing what the design record should SAY, with the build question already closed. The measurement, which either option must live with: the spec-to-folder mapping is not total (of 111 archived specs, 92 resolve to complete, 3 to cancelled, and 16 to nothing - 15 shared effort docs plus WI-300-sr052-binding.2026-07-26.md, whose name does not match _own_spec's own glob); it is contradictory for at least one file (research-knowledge.2026-07-29.md is cited from both terminal states, and R-F archives a shared doc when its LAST open citer closes, so both folders are correct for it); there is no regenerator to gate the derived location for freshness (gen_trajectory.py names 'archive' zero times); for the 92 attributable specs docs/work/ already answers shipped-or-cancelled by location; and no reader consumes the split - every one of them would have to widen its glob to ignore it. ON THE TIMING, so the record is not read as a criticism of the filing: WI-391 was correctly filed given the ruling it inherited, and refutation is exactly what a claimed row is for. The available improvement is only about WHERE the question gets asked. The intake said AT FILING, in its own words, that the row 'deletes no machinery, closes no raise path and makes no bad state unrepresentable' and 'must justify itself on the navigation benefit alone' - and section 0 prescribes asking 'what constraint would make this unrepresentable?' at FILING, where the cost is still comparable. Applied then, the answer was already 'none, by the row's own admission'. So this is the process working, one step later than section 0 prescribes.
BlastRadius: One sentence in docs/concurrency-v2.md B2, and the two docs/declared-absences entries that name the destinations and now point at this item. Nothing in docs/archive/specs/ moves under either option, so no link migration is incurred and no downstream repo is affected. Note one measured trap for whoever executes the ruling: the two declared-absences lines must be RESTATED, never deleted - deleting them adds +2 dangling references under check_doc_refs --strict, because the cancelled WI-391 spec's own title names both paths and stays in the registry permanently.
Options: (a) RESTATE - amend the sentence to record what the measurement found: the goal is met by the registry half for every attributable spec, and is unmeetable by any folder layout for the 16 that are not. FOR: the sentence's GOAL is sound and only its LOCATION is wrong, so restating preserves a correct intent while correcting a wrong mechanism; it leaves the 16 undecidable files named in the design record, which is the durable fact a future reader needs, since a flat docs/archive/specs/ will keep inviting the same tidy-up; and B2's own readers meet the correction where they meet the claim. AGAINST: it leaves a sentence that reads as a partial retreat rather than a clean decision, and it keeps text in a design doc describing something the repo deliberately does not do, which is its own kind of clutter. (b) STRIKE - delete the sentence outright. FOR: the kit's own state-it-once-and-link principle argues for deletion - the reasoning already has two homes (this item and the log fragment), so restating puts a third copy in the design doc; a design doc should describe the design, and this is no longer part of it; and a struck sentence cannot be misread later as a pending obligation, which a restated one can. AGAINST: B2's own readers then see no trace of the question, so the reasoning survives only where they are not looking - the tidy-up gets re-proposed by the next person to read a flat docs/archive/specs/, which is precisely how WI-391 came to be filed. (The claim that striking leaves 'no record of why' would be false - this item and the log fragment are that record - and the objection is narrower than that: it is about where the record is REACHABLE FROM.) (c) BUILD IT ANYWAY - accept a hand-adjudicated placement for the 16. FOR: B2 ships as written, and the navigation gain is real for anyone browsing the archive directly. AGAINST: it asserts a terminal state the repo does not hold for 14% of the corpus, has no honest answer at all for research-knowledge.2026-07-29.md, creates a second uncross-checked home for a fact the registry already carries, and adds a decision with a wrong-answer mode to every future close.
Recommendation: RESTATE (a). The goal in B2 is sound and is already achieved - a spec's shipped-or-cancelled IS answerable by location, at docs/work/ rather than at docs/archive/specs/ - so the sentence is wrong only in WHERE it puts the answer, and correcting it in place is a smaller and more honest edit than deleting it. The deciding argument against (b) is reachability rather than record-keeping: the 16 undecidable files do not go away, so a reader of a flat docs/archive/specs/ will reach for this tidy-up again, and B2 is where they will be reading. Weighed honestly, (b)'s state-it-once argument is the strongest case against this recommendation and a ruler may reasonably prefer it; the disagreement is narrow, and either way WI-391 stays cancelled.

Title: One machine-parseable carrier for the requirement registries - rule the .md + .csv split
OneLine: rule whether the four requirement tiers share ONE machine-parseable carrier - today SN is markdown prose and SR/LLR/TC are CSV, a split with no recorded rationale anywhere; recommendation is (b) one TOML carrier as the destination, sequenced as its own program after the repo is locked
Decision: Raised by the owner 2026-08-09 while scoping the attestation-anchor change (`docs/repo-lock.md` D-1 and F-7): why is SN a markdown file while the other three tiers are CSV? THE RATIONALE IS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE - searched `PROCESS.md`, `PROCESS_OPTIONS.md`, `ADOPTING.md`, `EXAMPLE.md`, `registry-machinery-reference.md`, the whole of `log.md`, and the archive. Every document DESCRIBES the consequence - -the one tier stored as prose, which changes almost everything about how it is validated- - and none justifies it. The form is inherited rather than chosen: the file was `registries/user-needs.template.md` before the SN rename, markdown from the start, and every later decision treated it as given - including the 2026-07-12 G1 ruling that picked section-as-state for SN maturity precisely because it was the -least schema churn- against a table that already existed. This item exists so the split is either RATIFIED as a decision or replaced, rather than continuing as an accident. NOTE THE CATEGORY, because it decides where this lands once ruled: this is NOT a stakeholder need - the owner's framing is -I do not really care how the data is stored- - it is a DESIGN CONSTRAINT, and the kit has no declared home for one. `PROCESS.md`'s G1 bar literally requires -usability/doc needs + constraints + non-goals captured-; non-goals have the `NG-` section in `stakeholder-needs.md`; constraints have no registry, no id space, and no ADR concept at all. In practice they are recorded as SNs - SN-003 (stack-agnostic), SN-011 (stdlib plus argued dependencies) and SN-012 (right-sized process) are all constraints, not desires - which is the shape this takes if it is ruled.
BlastRadius: MEASURED, and it differs sharply by option. Reading 32 SN rows costs about 166 code lines across 14 functions in 8 modules; reading all 436 SR+LLR+TC rows PLUS every off-spine registry costs `trace.load_csv`, five lines, because `csv.DictReader` does the rest - so the SN tier costs roughly 28x the parsing code for 7 percent of the rows, and it is also the only tier with no schema tier at all (no required-field checks, no enum checks - reference doc section 12.5). Two of those SN readers are F5 twins pinned equal by `tests/test_rule_sync.py`; a third pair, `traj_parse._sn_rows` and `gen_okf.sn_rows`, is pinned by nothing but a docstring saying -change both together- and HAS ALREADY DRIFTED ONCE, rendering a phantom SN-000 root in the dashboard icicle - a live hazard under every option, including keeping things as they are. Option (b) is a kit version bump with a downstream migration: every F5-duplicated loader, the shipped templates, `bootstrap.py` MAPPING, `EXAMPLE.md`, `ADOPTING.md`, `registry-machinery-reference.md` and the OKF export; `trace.structure_findings` (column-count integrity) has no analogue, though a parse error is arguably a stronger check; and `test_dogfood_sync`'s ordered-superset header rule has no meaning over TOML keys and needs redesigning. The precedent is IN-REPO and its cost is known rather than estimated: `work-items.csv` already became the `docs/work/` TOML-frontmatter spec folder, as a multi-phase program (2b, the 2c authority flip, Phase 5's deletion of the CSV home) spanning weeks, forcing a re-attestation sitting (LLR-051/056 re-grounded, SR-129/LLR-136 flipped Modified) and surfacing real defects - `build_scope_srs` and `critique_control` had been reading silently EMPTY since the 2c flip, which is the fail-open shape this kit exists to catch. A spine migration is LARGER than that one, because the WI registry carries no upward or downward joins into three sibling registries and the spine does. NOTHING HERE IS URGENT: D-1 and D-2 in `docs/repo-lock.md` are carrier-neutral - `TextDigest` and `AcceptedCommit` are FIELDS, not a format - so they survive any carrier, and ruling this later forecloses nothing.
Options: (a) KEEP THE SPLIT and ratify it as a decision, recording the rationale that was never written. FOR: zero cost and zero risk; the CSV tiers are read by five lines of stdlib and they work; a lock program exists to CLOSE the largest amendment window this repo has carried, and this would open a larger one on top of it. AGAINST: it ratifies an accident rather than a design; it leaves the 166-line SN reader and the unpinned `traj_parse`/`gen_okf` twin standing; and it leaves the SN tier - the one a G1 consistency review leans on hardest - with no schema tier at all. (b) ONE TOML CARRIER for all four tiers. FOR: `tomllib` is stdlib at the kit's declared 3.11 floor, so it costs no dependency - unlike a markdown parser, which `docs/dependencies.md` would have to admit as the first Python row ever, in the shipped tier the kit holds stdlib-preferred; the kit ALREADY sanctions TOML in two homes (`docs/process.toml` and the +++ frontmatter of every `docs/work` spec); multi-line basic strings dissolve every measured carrier defect at once; typed arrays retire `refs()` splitting on whitespace and with it the SN-001-and-SN-002 orphan bug (reference doc section 12.8); TOML carries COMMENTS, which CSV cannot - today the SR template fakes them by stuffing a 700-character explanation of the Phase rule inside an example row's cell value; and it unifies SN with the other three tiers behind one loader, deleting about 139 lines of bespoke parsing. AGAINST: `tomllib` is READ-ONLY (PEP 680 omitted a writer deliberately) and this kit writes registries programmatically - `intake` rewrites Status today and must write the anchor cells under D-1 - so it needs a third hand-rolled emitter or the first genuinely shared one; the repo already carries two, by two strategies that are NOT interchangeable (`wi_convert.toml_string` re-serializes and re-parses to verify; `bootstrap.set_process_key` does a line rewrite so the explanatory header survives, which works only because that file owes the git hooks one key per line); plus the kit version bump and downstream migration sized above. (c) MARKDOWN TABLES EVERYWHERE, for consistency with SN. FOR: one carrier, and the most directly readable in an editor. AGAINST: REFUTED ON MEASUREMENT - five live cells already contain a literal pipe character (SR-024, SR-043, LLR-024, LLR-040, LLR-152), which `traj_parse`'s naive split-on-pipe shape cannot survive; 552 cells contain commas, which CSV handles by RFC-4180 quoting and markdown has no equivalent for; the longest cell is 1553 characters; an embedded newline has no representation at all (none exist today, but the CSV form permits one and `gen_open_items.normalize` exists because a Windows-authored multi-line cell was observed); there is no analogue for `trace.structure_findings`; and there is no reusable markdown-table reader here to inherit - the `docs/work` loader parses no tables at all (it is `tomllib` over +++ fences, small BECAUSE the fields are TOML) and the SN tables are read by six bespoke scanners, two of which index cells POSITIONALLY, which is exactly the failure the column-count guard exists to catch.
Recommendation: (b) as the DESTINATION, (a) as the ACTION for this program - and those are not in conflict. The carrier question has a right answer and it is TOML: it is the only option that is stdlib at the declared floor, already sanctioned in two homes here, and able to hold the cells that actually exist rather than the cells one wishes existed. But the lock program's whole purpose is to close an open amendment window, and a kit-wide carrier migration inside it would open a bigger one - so rule the destination now if you are ready, and sequence the work as its own program once the repo is locked. IF (b) IS RULED: it graduates to an SN plus its SR on the SN-011 shape - a constraint recorded as a need, which is already what this kit does with stack-agnosticism and the dependency floor - and the F-8 gap, that a design constraint has no declared home at all, becomes worth its own row rather than a note. IF (a) IS RULED: record the rationale in `PROCESS.md` so the next reader does not re-derive it from scratch, as this one did. EITHER WAY, one thing is owed separately and should not wait on this ruling: the `traj_parse._sn_rows` / `gen_okf.sn_rows` twin is pinned by no test and has already drifted once, and that hazard is identical under all three options.
